13.0. Module Introduction
////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

Welcome to Module 14!

In this module you will be perfecting your ability to perform the basic cardiopulmonary examination procedures. You will be on campus in live lab sessions dedicated to demonstration, performance, and instructor feedback on completing each of the previously reviewed vitals. You will also be formally tested on your ability to obtain each of these vital signs, along with applying these vital signs to a patient case and determining exercise prescription parameters as a way to test your ability to synthesize and apply everything learned in Cardiopulmonary 1. 

Learning Objectives
By the end of this week, you will be able to: 

Perform brachial and radial heart rate, manual and automated blood pressure, respiratory rate, and pulse oximetry. 
Perform ankle brachial index with use of doppler ultrasound.
Perform and analyze blood pressure during positional changes better known of orthostatic blood pressure assessment. 
Describe and analyze vitals during exercise and determine if an abnormal or normal response has occurred.

        .Lab Competency Exam 10:00 – 12:00 pm:
            In lab immersion 1B you will be engaging in a lab competency. This require you to be fully prepared to demonstrate your skills in taking vital signs and explaining what you know regarding vitals assessment and patient response. Please review the following guidelines prior to the lab practical to ensure full understanding of how you will be graded and what you may expect during the assessment

        5 points. Answers question and/or performs technique correctly with minimal delay in response. Demonstrates appropriate patient approach including introduction, communication, preparation, and consent. No errors, or self corrects errors without prompting.  
            half points may be awarded based on instructor grading (IE: 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5)

        Testing Format:
            Each competency check is scheduled for 10 minutes. During the assessment one student will act as tester and one will act as patient. The tester will perform a vital signs assessment covered in this course: heart rate, blood pressure, orthostatic assessment, respiratory rate, and SpO2. You may have to perform all or a chosen few, so being prepared is important. You will also be asked some discussion pieces regarding normal or abnormal vital response, and/or therapist response to vital sign readings.

        Scoring:
            Each case will contain 7 associated tasks/questions, and the total points for the exam will be 35. Students must score at least 75% or >26/35 to receive a passing grade on the competency check.

        Debriefing:
            You and your instructor will briefly discuss key points and provide examples of areas of great performance and areas where performance could be improved. This will be brief and provide insight on your strengths and weaknesses noted during the lab practical session.

        Components:
            -You will take a set of vitals
            -Must have appropriate patient approach and communication
            -Correct steps and measurement techniques
            -Be prepared to be asked “what ifs,” as in, “what if the patient’s blood pressure is high?”
            -There are both demonstrative and verbal components, so be prepared to answer questions related to the patient or vitals being taken
            -Need to know normal for vitals
            -Modifications that may need to implement to obtain the vital
            -REVIEW ALL COMPOMPONENTS OF LAB MANUAL
            -See patient management 1 instructions for patient management component of lab practical
                See: 'PM.txt::'

Question 1
    A patient has been admitted to the hospital due to complaints of difficulty breathing. His ABGs report pH = 7.20, PaCO2 = 63.4, PaO2 = 51, HCO3– = 30; PFTs report TLC = 120% predicted, VC = 115% predicted, RV = 130% predicted, FEV1 = 48% predicted, and he has a concerning lab value of WBC = 15,000. A chest x-ray indicates hyperinflated lungs, but also large presence of infiltrates in the right lower lobe. Which of the following diagnostic conclusions BEST summarizes this patient’s condition? 
       
    a.The patient has pneumonia, acute respiratory acidosis, and severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
    b.The patient has atelectasis, acute respiratory alkalosis, and mild restrictive pulmonary disease.
    c.The patient has atelectasis, acute metabolic acidosis, and mild chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
    d.The patient has pneumonia, acute metabolic alkalosis, and severe restrictive pulmonary disease.
     
    a.The patient has pneumonia, acute respiratory acidosis, and severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

    Reduction in RV
    Increase in % FEV1

    Reduction in % FEV1

CARDIO FINAL MATCHING QUIZ 
    Pulmonary Condition 
        • Sarcoidosis 
        • Bacterial Pneumonia 
        • Bronchiolitis Obliterans 
        • Spinal Cord Injury 
        • Emphysema 
        • Viral Pneumonia 
        • Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) 
        • Pediatric Respiratory Distress Syndrome 
        • Pulmonary Embolism (PE) 
        • Ankylosing Spondylitis 
        • COPD 
        • Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis 
        • Pulmonary Edema 
        • Chronic Bronchitis 
        • Atelectasis 
        • Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) 
        • Bronchogenic Carcinoma 
        • Bronchiectasis 
        • Diaphragmatic Paralysis or Paresis 
        • Cystic fibrosis 
        • Kyphoscoliosis 
 
    Definition 
        • Partial or full occlusion of the pulmonary vasculature 
        • Mucus stasis in conducting airways of lung, nasal sinuses, sweat glands, small intestine, pancreas, and biliary system, abnormal salt and water transport, failure of airways to clear mucus normally, multisystem disorder, genetic mutation on chromosome 7, abnormal CFTR 
        • Characterized by necrosis of the respiratory epithelium in the affected bronchioles 
        • Malignant growth of abnormal epithelial cells in the bronchus 
        • Inflammation of the lung associated with aspiration, drug toxicity, inhalation injury, pulmonary trauma, shock, systemic infection, organ failures. Fluid builds up in the tiny, elastic air sacs (alveoli) in your lungs 
        • Progressive degenerative disease of the nervous system that involves both upper and lower motor neurons 
        • Inflammatory reaction of the distal airways from inhalation of bacteria, viruses, microorganisms, foreign substances, gastric contents, or complication of radiation therapy 
        • Partial or total collapse of alveoli, lung segments, lobes that can result from hypoventilation 
        • an increase in amount of fluid w/in the lungs resulting from excessive fluid movement from pulmonary vascular system to the extravascular system 
        • Inflammatory process of alveolar wall where lung becomes scarred 
        • Loss or impairment of motor function of diaphragm due to a lesion in the neurological or muscular system, elevated hemi-diaphragm 
        • This type will resolve from alterations and capillary permeability, intrapleural pressures from airway obstruction or lymph vessel obstruction, and is caused by changes in capillary permeability as a result of a direct or an indirect pathologic insult. 
        • Hyaline membrane disease, caused by abnormalities in surfactant system and inadequate surfactant production, disorder of prematurity or lack of complete lung maturation 
        • Associated with left ventricular failure when it’s no longer able to pump blood in systemic circulation and caused by increased pressures in the heart. 
        • Combination of excessive anteroposterior and lateral curvature of the thoracic spine 
        • Enigmatic multisystem disease characterized by the presence of noncaseating epithelioid granulomas in many organs 
        • Damage or interruption to the neurological pathways contained in the spinal cord mark spinal cord injury 
        • Chronic inflammatory disease of the spine characterized by immobility of sacroiliac and vertebral joints and ossification of paravertebral ligaments, inherited arthritic condition 
 
    Symptoms 
        • Cough, chest pain, unexplained weight loss, hypoxemia, hypocapnia, increased pH, respiratory restrictive diseases 
        • Presence of a chronic productive cough for 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years, excess in body fluids & chronic cough related to hypersecretions 
        • Tachypnea, hypotension, high HR, decreased chest wall expansion, altered mental status, ↓ PaO2 (<60 mm Hg), ↓ PaCO2, symmetric bilateral diffuse fluffy infiltrates on imaging 
        • Tachypnea, tachycardia, crackles at involved site, diminished breath sounds, dry or wet cough, diaphragmatic weakness, hypoxemia from V/Q mismatch, transpulmonary shunting, tracheal shift, opacification 
        • Cough with sputum production, secretion layers, hemoptysis, recurrent, chronic, or recurring lung infections, hypoxemia, dilated bronchioles, crackles or rhonchi 
        • Destruction of alveolar wall and enlargement of airspaces distal to bronchioles including respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts and alveoli 
        • Dilation of the bronchia, distortion of conducting airways, thickening, herniation, or dilation, localized or diffused 
        • Cough, respiratory infections, sinusitis and nasal polyps, pancreatic exocrine malfunction, malabsorption of important nutrients, those w/ intestinal & pancreatic involvement present w/ thin frame, low weight, muscle wasting, increased kyphosis, posterior pelvic 
        tilt 
        • Moderate fever, bilateral diffuse scattered fluffy shadows indicating patchy alveolar infiltrates, non-productive cough, normal WBC count, myalgia/muscle pain 
        • Crackles or wheeze, hypotension, tachycardia, diminished breath sounds, rapid onset of tachypnea, chest pain, lightheaded, medical emergency if suspected, no sputum 
        • CHF associated, basilar infiltrated on imaging, SOB, cyanotic, labored breathing, ↑ RR, ↓ PaO2, ↓ PaCO2, ↑ pH (respiratory alkalosis), Wet rales with ↓ breath sounds 
 
    Treatment / PT Management 
        • Patient proning & improve V/Q ratio 
        • Pursed lip breathing, smoking cessation, pharmacotherapy, pulmonary rehabilitation, surgical incision, oxygen therapy, dyspnea relief 
        • Blood in sputum = contraindication, secretion clearance techniques, postural drainage during flare-ups, inspiratory muscle training, strength training, controlled breathing techniques coordinated w/ activity 
        • Corticosteroids, cytotoxic drugs, smoking cessation, maintaining adequate oxygenation/ventilation, good nutrition, treatment of infection, lung transplantation 
        • Conservative w/ orthotic devices, surgical placement of Harrington distraction strut bars, preventative and supportive measures for pulmonary compromise 
        • Coughing techniques, supplemental O2 when low, prevention, positioning & postural drainage 
        • Prevention & deep breathing 
        • Active and passive chest wall stretches, strengthening, increase endurance of ventilatory muscles 
        • Support therapy & diaphragm motor pacing 
        • No cure; maintain good body alignment and thoracic mobility 
        • Secretion clearance techniques (postural drainage & coughing), thoracic stretching exercises, controlled breathing techniques, inspiratory muscle training, postural reeducation, monitor pulse oximetry 
        • Surfactant replacement therapy or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO); administration of corticosteroids to mother before birth

CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS
    Abdominal aortic aneurysm   
        ●   Pressure on surrounding parts ~ i.e., low back
        ●   Leg pain/claudication pain
        ●   Numbness in LE
        ●   Excessive fatigue
        ●   Poor distal pulses
        ●   Low back pain (LBP)

    Acinetobacter   
        ●   Ventilator associated pneumonia 
        ○   Fever
        ○   Increasing O2 requirement
        ○   Increased secretions
        ●   Bloodstream infections
        ○   Fever
        ○   Shock
        ○   Delirium
        ●   Meningitis (RARE)
        ○   Fever
        ○   Seizures

    Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) 
        ●   Tachypnea
        ●   Decreased chest wall expansion
        ●   Diminished breath sounds, crackles, wheezes
        ●   Hypotension 
        ●   High heart rate
        ●   Altered mental state
        ●   Symmetric bilateral diffuse fluffy infiltrates on imaging
        ●   Decreased PaO2 (<60 mmHg), decreased PaCO2
        ○   50 mmHg = mechanical ventilation required

    Angina pectoris     
        ●   Paroxysmal ~ current attacks of substernal chest discomfort (doesn’t occur all the time)
        ●   Transient ischemia
        ●   Relieved by rest ~ decreased O2 demand
        ●   Relieved by vasodilator medications
        ●   Substernal chest pain or pressure
        ●   Diaphoresis
        ●   SOB
        ●   Silent ~ can be caused by diabetes (pain is altered)

    Asthma  
        ●   Dyspnea ~ can’t get as much air in
        ●   Cough
        ●   Wheezing (expiratory) ~ hallmark of asthma
        ●   Chest tightness
        ●   Episodic - chest tightness
        ●   Clear triggers
        ●   Atrophy
        ○   Pale / edematous membranes nasopharynx (swollen)
        ○   Nasal polyps
        ○   Atopic dermatitis - red, itchy rash (wash hands often)

    Atelectasis     
        ●   Tachypnea ~ shallow breathing
        ●   Tachycardia
        ●   Crackles at involved site ~ diminished breath sounds
        ●   Dry or wet cough

    Bronchiectasis  
        ●   Productive cough (with different mucopurulent secretions)
        ●   Secretion layers - white frothy, mucoid inner, purulent bottom ~ composed of thick yellow-green plugs
        ●   Sputum is greatest in the morning
        ●   Recurrent, chronic, or recurring lung infections
        ●   Hemoptysis

    Bronchogenic carcinoma  
        ●   Cough
        ●   Chest pain
        ●   Unexpected weight loss
        ●   Metastases to other organs (cancerous growth)
        ●   Dyspnea
        ●   Hypoxemia (decreased PaO2)
        ●   Hypocapnia (decreased PaCO2)
        ●   Increased pH

    Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)    
        ●   Chronic bronchitis
        ○   Use of accessory muscles to breathe ~ patient may look to be “malnourished” 
        ○   Pursed-lip breathing
        ○   Leaning forward to breathe
        ○   Dyspnea on exertion (late sign) 
        ●   Emphysema 
        ○   Excess body fluids ~ patient may look as though they have a “beer belly”
        ○   Chronic cough, SOB on exertion
        ○   Increased sputum
        ○   Cyanosis (late sign)
        ●   General signs
        ○   Lung hyperinflation 
        ○   Elevation of shoulder girdle
        ○   Horizontal ribs
        ○   Barrel-shaped thorax/chest ~ seen on an x-ray
        ○   Low, flattening diaphragms
        ○   Delayed and incomplete emptying of the lung during exhalation ~ larger total lung capacities (TLC)
        ○   Two forced expiratory volumes monitored: FEV1 & FVC
        ●   Clinical signs
        ○   Abnormal ABGs
        ■   Decreased PaO2, increased PaCO2
        ■   Respiratory acidosis
        ○   Dyspnea on exertion ~ more noticeable during functional activities
        ○   Secretion production and cough (productive cough)
        ○   Increased anxiety level (potentially)
        ○   Breath sounds
        ■   Wheezing with retained secretions
        ■   Rhonchi or low-pitched rattling ~ large airway obstruction with secretions along airways 
        ■   Crackles or bubbling with presence of secretions
        ■   Prolonged expiration 
        ○   Decreased or poor exercise tolerance ~ reduction in exercise capacity on testing
        ○   Postural changes
        ■   Forward leaning with hands supported
        ■   Permanent changes to the thorax

    Clostridioides difficile (C. diff)  
        ●   Mild - moderate watery diarrhea (rarely bloody)
        ●   Cramping abdominal pain
        ●   Anorexia ~ loss of appetite
        ●   Malaise ~ generally feeling unwell 
        ●   Fever ~ more likely in more severe cases
        ●   May form yellow plaques on colon lining
        ○   Pseudomembranous colitis

    Congestive heart failure    
        ●   Crackles ~ happen during inspiration
        ●   Heart sounds ~ 3rd heart sound (noncompliant left ventricle)
        ○   Occurs during diastole after S2
        ●   Peripheral edema ~ fluid retention
        ○   Pitting edema
        ●   Jugular venous distention ~ comes from fluid overload
        ●   Pulsus alternans ~ alteration of femoral or radial pulse
        ●   Changes in extremities ~ cold skin, pale appearance, cyanotic
        ●   Weight gain ~ from increase in fluid volume
        ●   Sinus tachycardia
        ●   Decreased exercise tolerance

    COVID-19    
        ●   Asymptomatic
        ●   Fever
        ●   Cough
        ●   SOB
        ●   Fatigue
        ●   Myalgias
        ●   Headache
        ●   Loss of taste/smell
        ●   Congestion 
        ●   Nausea / vomiting
        ●   Diarrhea 

    Cystic fibrosis 
        ●   General 
        ○   Cough
        ○   Respiratory infections
        ○   Sinusitis and nasal polyps
        ●   GI complications
        ○   Pancreas, gallbladder, and intestinal tract disease
        ■   Pancreatic exocrine malfunction
        ■   Malabsorption of important nutrients including fat and protein
        ■   Biliary tract obstruction 
        ●   Reproductive and/or musculoskeletal systems may be affected

    Endocarditis    
        ●   Fever
        ●   Malaise
        ●   Night sweats
        ●   Weight loss
        ●   Heart murmur
        ●   Vascular phenomena
        ○   Septic emboli ~ lung and brain
        ○   Janeway lesions
        ○   Splinter hemorrhages
        ●   Immunologic phenomena
        ○   Roth spots
        ○   Osler nodes
        ○   Glomerulonephritis 

    Heart failure   
        ●   Dyspnea
        ●   Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea ~ unexplained episodes of SOB that occur in supine position
        ●   Orthopnea ~ development of dyspnea in recumbent position
        ●   Breathing patterns ~ shallow but quick breaths
        ●   Radiological findings in congestive heart failure
        ○   Size of cardiac silhouette evaluation
        ○   Fluid in the lungs ~ interstitial, perivascular, alveolar edema
        ●   Echocardiography
        ○   Ejection fraction ~ reduced or preserved (left ventricle)
        ○   Left ventricle structure
        ○   Other structural abnormalities
        ●   Lab values in congestive heart failure
        ○   ANP and BNP
        ○   Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
        ○   Liver enzymes (AST, bilirubin, LDH-5)
        ○   Kidney markers (BUN, creatinine)
        ○   ABGs ~ related to kidney and lung dysfunction
        ●   Dry cough
        ●   Edema (LE)
        ●   Abdominal pain
        ●   Reduce cardiac output
        ○   Fatigue
        ○   Weakness
        ○   Activity intolerance 

    Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)  
        ●   Early
        ○   Fever
        ○   Headache
        ○   Fatigue
        ○   Lymphadenopathy (swollen lymph nodes)
        ●   Late
        ○   Weight loss
        ○   Night sweats
        ○   Extreme fatigue
        ○   Sores and blotches on mucus and skin (looks of cancer)

    Hypertension    
        ●   Asymptomatic
        ●   Hypertensive emergency
        ○   Headache
        ○   Vision changes
        ○   Chest pain
        ○   SOB
        ○   Back pain

    Influenza   
        ●   Fever (<101)
        ●   Cough
        ●   Sore throat
        ●   SOB 
        ●   Myalgias ~ extreme muscle aches
        ●   Fatigue
        ●   headache

    Interstitial lung disease   
        ●   Dyspnea ~ impaired gas exchange due to the fibrotic of septa in the parenchyma
        ●   Dry cough (compared to bronchitis)
        ●   Hemoptysis 
        ●   Bibasilar inspiratory crackles (velcro) ~ at bottom of lungs
        ●   Extrapulmonary symptoms
        ○   Chest pain
        ○   MSK pain
        ○   Fatigue
        ○   Arthralgia 

    Legionella pneumophila  
        ●   Fever
        ●   Cough
        ●   Sputum
        ●   SOB
        ●   Nausea
        ●   Vomiting
        ●   Diarrhea 

    Methicillin resistant staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)  
        ●   Cellulitis / septic arthritis ~ classic signs of infection
        ○   Erythema 
        ○   Edema
        ○   Calor
        ○   Rubor
        ○   Abscess formation 
        ●   Other areas
        ○   Osteomyelitis
        ○   Bacteremia
        ○   Endocarditis
        ○   Pneumonia 
        ●   these are dependent on where the infection is located

    Myocardial infarction (MI)  
        ●   Diaphoresis ~ excessive sweating
        ●   Tachycardia
        ●   Tachypnea
        ●   New murmur or mitral regurgitation
        ●   S3 and S4 heart sounds
        ●   can be either an NSTEMI or STEMI

    Norovirus   
        ●   Lasts 24-72 hours
        ●   Nausea
        ●   Vomiting
        ●   Diarrhea
        ●   Abdominal cramps
        ●   Low grade fever
        ●   Headache ~ from dehydration
        ●   Myalgias ~ from dehydration
        ●   Malaise ~ from dehydration 

    Orthostatic hypotension 
        ●   Lightheadedness
        ●   Dizziness
        ●   Blurry or tunnel vision 
        ●   Syncope 

    Pericarditis    
        ●   Chest pain
        ○   Sharp
        ○   Relieved by sitting up and leaning forward
        ○   Words with inspiration / coughing
        ●   Pericardial friction rub
        ●   EKG: ST segment elevation in all leads
        ●   Pericardial effusion 

    Peripheral arterial disease 
        ●   Intermittent claudication ~ painful walking, pain in LE 
        ○   Reproducible muscular pain with activity
        ○   Relieved with rest (10 minutes)
        ○   Varies in severity
        ○   Buttock, hip, thigh, calf, foot
        ●   Ischemic rest pain
        ○   Forefoot and toes
        ○   Worse with elevation 
        ●   Increased pallor with foot elevation
        ●   Decreased venous filling after elevation 
        ●   Dependent rubor ~ redness of distal limb
        ●   Gangrene ~ necrotic tissue
        ●   Ischemic ulcers
        ○   Trauma ~ poor healing due to lack of blood supply
        ○   Toe joints, bony prominence, anterior shin, base of heel
        ○   “Punched out” irregular margins, dry base
        ○   Painful ~ due to nerves not getting enough blood
        ●   Drier or shiny skin
        ●   Hair loss
        ●   Thickened toenails
        ●   Muscle atrophy
        ●   Decreased sensation
        ●   Cool
        ●   Long capillary refill
        ●   Atypical extremity pain
        ●   Decreased peripheral pulses ~ tibial or dorsalis pedis arteries
        ●   Abnormal ABI readings ~ </= 0.90

    Peripheral vascular disease 
        ●   Dull ache, burning, fatigue while standing
        ●   Itching
        ●   Tingling
        ●   Heaviness, night cramping
        ●   Elevation and walking reduce symptoms
        ●   Swollen lower limbs
        ●   Normal muscle mass
        ●   Warm skin, hyperpigmented or dermatitis, and hemosiderin staining (visible skin changes)
        ○   For chronic venous insufficiency
        ○   Hemosiderin - occurs when RBCs lead into the tissue secondary to venous hypertension
        ●   Venous wounds ~ beefy and red in color
        ○   Mild-to-moderate severe exudate and irregular borders

    Pneumonia   
        ●   Bacterial
        ○   Abrupt onset
        ○   Lobar consolidation in one or more lobes
        ○   High fever and chills
        ○   Productive cough ~ pleuritic pain
        ○   Dyspnea, tachypnea 
        ○   High WBC count
        ●   Viral
        ○   Bilateral diffuse ~ scattered fluffy shadows indicating patchy alveolar infiltrates
        ○   Moderate fever
        ○   Myalgia or muscle pain
        ○   Non-productive cough
        ○   Normal WBC count
        ●   General
        ○   Decreased lung volumes, decreased lung compliance, decreased gas exchange, increased respiratory rate, increased work of breathing
        ○   Decreased PaO2, may have decreased PaCO2 as a result of breathing pattern of blowing off CO2
        ○   Absent breath sounds over area of pneumonia
        ○   Increased heart rate (presence of fever) ~ typically

    Pulmonary edema 
        ●   Basilar infiltrates on imaging
        ●   Decreased PaO2, decreased PaCO2, increased pH (respiratory alkalosis)
        ●   Wet rales with decreased breath sounds
        ●   SOB, cyanotic, increased respiratory rate, labored breathing

    Pulmonary embolism  
        ●   SOB
        ●   Drop in SpO2
        ●   Chest pain ~ rapid onset
        ●   Cough
        ●   Sudden tachycardia
        ●   can start as deep vein thrombosis
        ●   Rapid onset of feeling lightheaded
        ●   Hypotension
        ●   Decreased chest
        ●   Diminished breath sounds ~ distal to PE
        ●   Crackles or wheeze ~ potentially!
        ●   No sputum
        ●   PE is a MEDICAL EMERGENCY even if it is suspected!!

    Tuberculosis (TB)   
        ●   Fever
        ●   Night sweats
        ●   Weight loss and anorexia ~ loss of appetite
        ●   Malaise and weakness
        ●   Cough (pulmonary TB)
        ○   Initially non reproductive
        ○   Eventually purulent (pus-filled)
        ○   Blood streaked sputum
        ●   Lymph node TB
        ○   Painless enlarged lymph nodes
        ●   Pleural TB
        ○   TB bacilli escape into pleural cavity
        ○   Pleural chest pain and effusions
        ●   Miliary TB
        ○   Hematogenous spread
        ○   Affect other organs that get a lot of blood (kidney, liver, spleen) ~ potentially!

    Urinary tract infection (UTI)   
        ●   Dysuria (pain with urination)
        ●   Frequency
        ●   Urgency ~ not much comes out
        ●   Hematuria (blood in urine)
        ●   Suprapubic pain ~ sometimes above pubic symphysis
        ●   Flank pain (in kidneys)
        ●   Progression to urosepsis
        ○   Blood stream infection
        ○   Fever
        ○   Chills
        ○   Delirium
        ○   Shock

    Venous insufficiency    
        ●   Telangiectasis (spider veins)
        ●   Dilated intradermal venules 
        ●   more common in women
        ●   Varicose veins
        ●   Subcutaneous dilated tortuous veins
        ●   >/= 3mm when standing
        ●   Cosmetically undesirable
        ●   Physically uncomfortable 
        ●   LE discomfort ~ heavy feeling
        ●   LE pain
        ●   LE edema
        ●   Skin discoloration
        ●   Stasis dermatitis
        ●   itching

    RISK FACTORS
        Abdominal aortic aneurysm   
            ●   Smoking (current or past)
            ●   Age
            ●   Gender
            ●   Family history
            ●   Hypertension
            ●   Hyperlipidemia
            ●   Atherosclerosis 

        Acinetobacter
            ●   Crucial illness (ICU)
            ●   Prolonged hospital stay / long term residence care facility
            ●   Tubes / lines / drains
            ●   Broad spectrum antibiotic use

        Asthma 
            ●   Prenatal / childhood
            ○   Genetics
            ○   Prenatal exposure to maternal smoking
            ○   Kids: AMAB (assigned male at birth)
            ○   Atopy / allergies
            ○   Air pollution
            ○   Obesity 
            ●   Adult
            ○   Obesity 
            ○   Smoking
            ■   Active
            ■   Second Hand
            ■   Can be associated with emphysema and bronchitis
            ○   Occupational exposures
            ■   Bakers - from aerosolized wheat in the air from flour
            ■   Health care workers - due to aerosolized medications
            ■   Auto-worker - from chemicals
            ■   Hairdressers - from chemicals

        Atherosclerosis     
            ●   Hyperlipidemia
            ●   Hypertension
            ●   Smoking
            ●   Diabetes
            ●   Obesity
            ●   Obstructive sleep apnea
            ●   Inactivity
            ●   Age
            ●   Family history
            ●   Stress (chronic)
            ●   Alcohol use

        Cardiovascular disease  
            ●   Behavioral
            ○   Smoking
            ○   Physical activity ~ physical inactivity, reduced aerobic exercise 
            ○   Healthy diet
            ○   Normal body weight
            ●   Health management
            ○   Blood pressure ~ higher in sedentary people
            ○   Cholesterol ~ higher in sedentary people
            ○   Fasting blood glucose
            ●   Genetics 
            ●   Gender 
            ●   Undiagnosed CHD 
            ○   Age ~ stiffer and less compliant arteries 
            ○   SBP ~ elevated
            ○   Left ventricular hypertrophy
            ○   Intraventricular block on ECG ~ heart block Type 2
            ○   Nonspecific ECG abnormalities
            ○   Serum cholesterol ~ elevated; damaging effects of the fats on arterial lining of arteries
            ○   Heart rate ~ elevated at resting
            ○   Vital capacity ~ low; particularly seen in females
            ○   Cigarettes consumed daily ~ accounts for 15% of HD
            ■   4/day → CVD
            ○   Relative weight ~ BMI >30kg/m2
            ●   Diagnosed CHD
            ○   Decreased left ventricular ejection fraction 
            ●   Type A behavior (stress) ~ increases HR for fight-or-flight response
            ○   Increases catecholamine secretion in the body which is a precursor for platelet aggregation

        Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)    
            ●   Inhalation factors
            ○   Smoking
            ○   Chemicals
            ○   Toxins
            ●   Genetics
            ○   Alpha-1 - antitrypsin deficiency 

        Chronic venous insufficiency or peripheral venous disease   
            ●   Advanced age
            ●   Genetics
            ●   Obesity
            ●   Prolonged standing
            ●   Sedentary lifestyle
            ●   Smoking
            ●   Female hormones

        Clostridioides difficile (C. diff)  
            ●   Previous antibiotic use
            ○   Broad spectrum antibiotics
            ○   Fluoroquinolones
            ●   Patient factors
            ○   Prolonged hospitalization
            ○   Comorbidities ~ end stage kidney disease
            ○   Advanced age (>65)
            ○   Immunocompromised ~ cancer, transplant
            ○   GI surgery ~ or other stress to the system

        Coronary artery disease (CAD)   
            ●   Hyperlipidemia
            ●   Hypertension
            ●   Smoking
            ●   Diabetes
            ●   Obesity
            ●   Sleep apnea
            ●   Inactivity
            ●   Age
            ●   Family history
            ●   Stress 
            ●   Alcohol 

        COVID-19    
            ●   Age
            ●   Cancer
            ●   Chronic diseases (lung, liver, or kidney)
            ●   Heart conditions
            ●   BMI >30
            ●   Pregnancy
            ●   Diabetes mellitus
            ●   Smoking
            ●   Transplant
            ●   HIV
            ●   Mental health disorders
            ●   Substance use disorders
            ●   Immunosuppressive medications

        Endocarditis    
            ●   Age >60
            ●   Male sex
            ●   Injection drug use
            ●   Structural heart disease
            ○   HCM
            ○   Valvular disease (rheumatic heart disease, prosthetic valves)
            ○   Congenital heart disease

        Heart failure   
            ●   Hypertension
            ●   Coronary artery disease
            ●   Cardiac dysrhythmias
            ●   Heart valve abnormality ~ valvular heart disease
            ●   Pulmonary embolism
            ●   Pulmonary hypertension
            ●   Renal failure
            ●   Spinal cord injury
            ●   Age-related changes
            ●   Smoking 
            ●   Obesity 
            ●   Diabetes 

        Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)  
            ●   MSM (men who have sex with men)
            ●   Injection drug use
            ●   Sex workers
            ●   Unprotected intercourse 

        Hypertension    
            ●   Dietary
            ●   Sodium excess
            ●   Stress
            ●   Obesity
            ●   Alcohol consumption
            ●   Inactivity 
            ●   Age
            ●   Family history

        Influenza   
            ●   Unvaccinated
            ●   Advanced age (>65)
            ●   Pregnant and postpartum women
            ●   Extreme obesity
            ●   Chronic medical conditions (lung, heart, diabetes)
            ●   Residing in long term care facility (prone to outbreaks)
            ●   Taking medications that affect immune system 

        Legionella pneumophila  
            ●   Advanced age
            ●   Immunocompromised
            ●   Comorbidities ~ heart disease, lung disease, renal disease
            ●   Smoking ~ chronic lung trauma
            ●   Exposure to contaminated man-made reservoirs

        Methicillin resistant staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)  
            ●   Direct contact with colonized surfaces or people
            ●   Colonizer 
            ○   Nares (nose)
            ○   Skin
            ○   Vagina
            ○   Oropharynx (mouth and pharynx)
            ●   Colonization
            ○   Diabetes patients on insulin
            ○   Human immunodeficiency virus - positive (HIV+)
            ○   Hemodialysis patients
            ○   Intravenous drug abusers
            ○   Patients with chronic skin lesions
            ●   Infection: immune deficiency or physiologic stress
            ○   Diabetes on insulin
            ○   Low WBC count
            ○   Chronic auto-immune problems
            ○   Neutropenia (decreased neutrophil count)
            ○   Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)
            ○   Corticosteroid therapy 
            ○   Chronic skin disease or trauma
            ■   IV drug users
            ■   Lacerations or abrasions
            ●   Hospital acquired
            ○   Antibiotics ~ increase resistant strain of staph.
            ○   Prolonged hospitalization / ICU
            ○   Catheter use
            ○   Patients with prosthetics ~ can infect surgery site
            ○   Surgical and/or burn patients 

        Myocardial infarction (acute coronary syndrome) ~ MI    
            ●   Increase chance for MI
            ○   Smoking
            ○   Hypercholesterolemia
            ○   Hypertension
            ○   Diabetes
            ○   Obesity
            ○   Stress
            ○   Family history
            ●   Decrease chance for MI
            ○   Daily consumption of fruits and vegetables
            ○   Regular alcohol consumption (1 drink/day)
            ○   Regular physical activity 

        Norovirus   
            ●   Outbreaks 
            ○   Restaurants
            ○   Health care facilities
            ○   School
            ●   Age ~ more common in pediatrics

        Peripheral arterial disease (PAD)   
            ●   Age
            ●   Male sex
            ●   Smoking
            ●   Diabetes
            ●   CV disease
            ●   Hyperlipidemia
            ●   Hypertension
            ●   Obesity 
            ●   Chronic kidney disease
            ●   Inactivity
            ●   Ethnicity
            ●   HIV infection ~ higher in positive compared to negative

        Pneumothorax    
            ●   Trauma or rib fracture ~ flail chest is a medical emergency
            ●   COPD
            ●   Tall people

        Tuberculosis    
            ●   Poverty
            ●   Poor access to healthcare
            ●   Immunocompromised
            ○   HIV
            ●   Institutionalized ~ large groups in poorly ventilated areas

        Venous insufficiency    
            ●   Age
            ●   Family history
            ●   Prolonged standing
            ●   BMI
            ●   Smoking
            ●   Pregnancy 

        Vancomycin resistant enterococcus (VRE) 
            ●   Previous antibiotic use
            ○   Vancomycin 
            ○   Broad spectrum antibiotics
            ●   Patient factors
            ○   Prolonged hospitalization
            ○   Comorbidities
            ■   Cancer
            ■   Transplant
            ○   Critical illness
            ○   Indwelling devices
            ■   Catheters ~ various types
            ■   Drains
            ■   Tubes from outside to inside the body
            ○   Colonization pressure
            ■   More patients colonized = higher risk for infection

    DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS
        Peripheral arterial disease vs lumbar radiculopathy 
            ●   PAD: symptoms occur during and physical exertion and diminished with rest
            ●   Lumbar radiculopathy: pain associated with nerve root compression and lead to distal aching; pain may be similar to PAD

    CARDIOMYOPATHY
        Diastolic heart failure (thick heart walls) 
            ●   Ejection fraction is preserved (HFpEF)
            ●   Left ventricle is decreased in size (hypertrophy) or there’s chronic replacement by fibrous tissue

        Systolic heart failure (thin heart walls)   
            ●   Ejection fraction is reduced (HFrEF) (~40%)
            ●   Left ventricle is stretched out or enlarged
            ●   Results in an increase in end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes

        Dilated 
            ●   Dilation of ventricles
            ●   Normal ventricular wall thickness
            ●   Progress to overall heart enlargement

        Hypertrophic    
            ●   Left ventricular hypertrophy
            ○   Increased voltage S wave V1-V3
            ○   Increased voltage R wave V4-V6
            ●   Increased left ventricular wall thickness
            ●   Decreased cavity size (smaller chamber)

        Hypertrophic obstructive    
            ●   Asymmetric interventricular septum (IVS) hypertrophy
            ●   Obstructs blood flow through the left ventricle outflow tract (LVOT)

        Restrictive     
            ●   Primary
            ○   Normal or decreased volume of both ventricle
            ○   Normal left ventricle wall thickness
            ○   Stiff walls ~ impaired ventricular filling
            ●   Acquired 
            ○   Myocarditis
            ○   Stress
            ○   Peripartum
            ○   Prolonged tachycardia
            ●   Secondary
            ○   Due to systemic disease process
            ■   Infiltrative → amyloidosis
            ■   Inflammatory → sarcoidosis
            ■   Endocrine → DM, thyroid disease
            ■   Neuromuscular → muscular dystrophy
            ■   Autoimmune → lupus (SLE)
            ■   Toxins → chemo

    PULMONARY DIAGNOSTIC TESTING
        Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis   
            ●   What can be assessed
            ○   pH - by the kidneys and lungs and can be compensated/uncompensated/partially compensated metabolic/respiratory acidosis/alkalosis
            ○   Ventilation
            ○   Oxygenation
            ●   GOLD STANDARD - better than using a pulse ox

        Body/Blood gas analysis 
            ●   Important for ABG readings including:
            ○   Arterial pH
            ○   PaCO2, PaO2
            ○   SpO2 - associated with oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve
            ○   HCO3
            ○   Excess of base
            ●   Helps with determining problems related to ventilation and oxygenation 
            ●   Blood gas analysis is important for
            ○   Kidneys and lungs, and determining the status the patient

        Bronchogram 
            ●   X-ray with bronchiectasis
            ●   Prominent, thick bronchial markings in right paracardiac regions of the lungs (to the right of the heart)

        Bronchography   
            ●   Evaluation and management of some congenital pulmonary abnormalities
            ○   Same for acquired diseases of tracheobronchial tree

        Chest radiograph    
            ●   What can be seen
            ○   Air
            ■   Dark to bone
            ○   Fat
            ○   Water
            ○   Bone
            ●   Views taken
            ○   Posteroanterior (PA)
            ○   Left lateral
            ○   Other
            ■   Decubitus
            ■   Lordotic
            ■   Oblique
            ■   AP at bedside
            ●   What is being assessed
            ○   Bones and soft tissues (thorax, ribs, diaphragm/hila)
            ○   Mediastinum, trachea, CV system
            ○   Lung fields
            ■   Vascular patterns
            ■   Alveolar patterns
            ■   Interstitial patterns
            ●   Assessment
            ○   Show diffuse alveolar filling pattern (prominent in middle and lower lung fields)
            ○   CXR indicating severe pulmonary edema
            ○   “Bat wing” infiltrate
            ●   Interpretation 
            ○   Eval location of all catheters, tubes, hemodynamic support devices
            ○   Assess CV status of patient
            ○   Check for abnormal parenchymal opacities 
            ○   Look for pleural effusions
            ○   Compare with previous studies or imaging

        Computed tomography (CT)    
            ●   What can be seen
            ○   Tumors
            ○   Calcifications
            ○   Nodules
            ○   Pulmonary embolism (helical CT)
            ○   Lungs
            ○   Heart
            ○   Mediastinum
            ○   Pleura
            ○   Chest wall
            ○   Upper abdomen
            ○   Detection of:
            ■   Pneumothorax
            ■   Effusions
            ○   Chest tube placement
            ○   Unsuspected abnormalities

        Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)    
            ●   Indicated for evaluation of chest wall processes
            ●   May be indicated in those with an abnormal chest radiograph that shows a nodule or mass

        Pulmonary arteriography 
            ●   GOLD STANDARD
            ●   What can be seen
            ○   Emboli:
            ■   Complete obstruction 
            ■   Intraluminal filling defects
            ■   Decrease in flow rate

        Pulmonary function testing (PFT)    
            ●   Measures the lungs’ ability to take air in and move it out
            ●   Can determine if someone has an obstructive or restrictive pulmonary condition

        Pulse oximetry  
            ●   Measures how much oxygen is bound to hemoglobin 
            ●   Provides a quick measurement but has specific limitations and other influential variables

        Ventilation and perfusion scans (V/Q)   
            ●   Used to measure regional distribution of pulmonary blood flow in lungs
            ●   Indicated to rule out pulmonary emboli
            ●   Inhale xenon gas → scan taken over lungs while breath is held to see any defects 

            ~ IMPORTANT TO NOTE that if a patient has right sided heart failure, they will ultimately have left sided heart failure
            ~ Patient education is KEY in preventing other or have recurring events from happening in the future

From an email after the final exam
    We wanted to give you some final exam information now that the grades are posted. You all did a great job! The class average was 87% and the range of scores 64% - 100%. We gave everyone 5 points back on your total scores, which include 4 questions with <50% correct stats and one typo. The question with the typo was: 
        ↓ PaO, ↑ PaCO2, ↑ pH is MOST associated with which of the following conditions? This should have read low pH to lead you to think respiratory acidosis and then correctly answering the only obstructive condition in the answer list being chronic bronchitis. We will review some of the others in cardio 2.

Final Exam Review and Open Q+A Γ2024
    Purpose of today’s review
        • Give some study areas of focus
        • Allow for you to ask questions regarding content or areas of struggle
        • Realize these are themes or areas of focus, but all content is important for the exam 

    Final Exam
        • 65 questions + 10 class submitted = 75 questions total
        • December 12th
        • Open 8 am – 8 pm
        • 2.5-hour time limit
        • Comprehensive 

    Comprehensive 
        • Pulmonary conditions, ABGs, SpO2/O2
        • CP Implications Associated with other Dx
        • CV Conditions
        • Lab Values 
        • Dx Imaging (Pulm and CV)
        • ECG

    Cardiovascular Conditions
        • Congestive Heart Failure
        • Systolic vs diastolic – all distinguishing features
        • Define dilated, hypertrophic, restrictive and idiopathic cardiomyopathy
        • Right sided heart failure or Cor Pulmonole
        • Common Vascular Conditions – PAD, PVD, DVT
        • HTN, Angina, MI

    Pulmonary Conditions
        • Pulmonary definitions (IE: hypoxia)
        • Features associated with restrictive vs obstructive lung conditions
        • Dx testing (know associated PFTs!)
        • Patient hallmark symptoms
        • Breathing patterns
        • ABGs
        • Common treatments associated with pulmonary conditions

    Pulmonary Conditions 
        • Restrictive lung dysfunction
            • Bacterial and viral pneumonia
            • ARDS
            • PE
            • Pulmonary edema (know the types)
            • Atelectasis
            • Neurological, MSK, and other causes 

        • Obstructive lung disease/disfunction 
            • COPD
            • Chronic bronchitis
            • Emphysema
            • Bronchiectasis 
            • Cystic fibrosis 

    Dx Imaging
        • Recognize (images from slides), understand, why or when they may be used in CV and Pulmonary Cases:
        • Cardiac catheterization
        • Echocardiography
        • CT scanning 
        • Chest X-ray
        • Ventilation-Perfusion Scan
        • MRI

    Lab Values
        • Lab values to review
        • CBC panel
        • Coagulation profiles and associated anti-coagulant
        • Lab values associated with what system
        • Electrolyte panel – be familiar 
        • ABGs
        • Know definitions of each lab value 
        • What are the cell types and what do they mean
        • PT implications

    ECGs
        • Common strips
        • Name the rhythm
        • 1 strip for counting 
        • Associating that strip/rhythm with a description 

    Other Systems & Cardiovascular Implications
        • Kidney Disease
        • Metabolic Disorders
        • Liver Disease 
        • Diabetes

    Other 
        • Understand SpO2
        • Relationship between SpO2 and PaO2

Symptom presentations - lab values
    Agitation   
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L)
        Hypocalcemia (calcium)

    Anemia  
        Leukopenia (WBC <4,000)

    Angina  
        Polycythemia (hemoglobin trending upward)
        Thrombocytosis (platelets >450,000)

    Anxiety     
        Hypocalcemia (calcium)

    Appetite    
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL) ~ poor
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward) ~ loss

    Back pain
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward)
        
    Bleeding    
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000)
        Thrombocytopenia (platelets <150,000) ~ risk

    Bones   
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL) ~ pain

    Bradycardia     
        Hyperkalemia (potassium >5.5mEq/L)

    Cardiac conditions  
        Hypercalcemia (calcium) ~ ventricular dysrhythmias, heart block, asystole
        Hyperkalemia (potassium >5.5mEq/L) ~ heart block, ventricular fibrillation, cardiac arrest
        Hypocalcemia (calcium) ~ EKG changes
        Hypokalemia (potassium <3.5mEq/L) ~ EKG changes, cardiac arrest
        Polycythemia (hemoglobin trending upward) ~ arrhythmias

    Clotting risk   
        Thrombocytosis (platelets >450,000)

    Cognition   
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL) ~ decreased
        Hypocalcemia (calcium) ~ confusion 
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L) ~ confusion
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward) ~ confusion

    Coma    
        Hypercalcemia (calcium)
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L)
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)

    Constipation    
        Hypercalcemia (calcium)
        Hypokalemia (potassium <3.5mEq/L)

    Control     
        Hypoglycemia (glucose <70) ~ loss

    Cramps  
        Hypocalcemia (calcium) ~ muscle
        Hypokalemia (potassium <3.5mEq/L) ~ leg
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)

    Diabeteic ketoacidosis (DKA)    
        Hyperglycemia (glucose >200mg/dL)

    Diarrhea    
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)

    Dizziness   
        Anemia
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000)
        Polycythemia (hemoglobin trending upward)
        Thrombocytosis (platelets >450,000)

    Dyspnea     
        Anemia
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL)
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward)

    Ecchymosis  
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000)
        Thrombocytopenia (platelets <150,000)

    Exercise    
        Anemia / downward trend of hemoglobin ~ decreased endurance and tolerance to activity

    Fatigue     
        Anemia (vague)
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL)
        Hyperglycemia (glucose >200mg/dL) ~ severe
        Hypocalcemia (calcium)
        Leukopenia (WBC <4,000)
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward)
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending downward) ~ uncommon; can be precursor to autoimmune disease
        Thrombocytopenia (platelets <150,000)

    Fever   
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000) 
        Leukopenia (WBC <4,000)
        Neutropenia (WBC <1,500) ~ low grade
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward) ~ low

    Fluid retention     
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL)
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L)

    Headache    
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)
        Leukopenia (WBC <4,000)
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward)
        Thrombocytosis (platelets >450,000)

    HTN 
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL)
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L)

    Irritability    
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L)
        Hypoglycemia (glucose <70)

    Jaundice    
        Thrombocytopenia (platelets <150,000)

    Joints  
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000) ~ painful and/or inflamed

    Lethargy / lethargic    
        Hypercalcemia (calcium)
        Hypoglycemia (glucose <70)
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000)

    Lymphadenopathy     
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000)

    Malaise     
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000)

    Nausea / vomiting   
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL)
        Hypercalcemia (calcium)
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)

    Orthostatic hypotension     
        Hypokalemia (potassium <3.5mEq/L)
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)
        Polycythemia (hemoglobin trending upward) ~ orthostasis

    Pallor  
        Anemia / downward trend of hemoglobin

    Paresthesia     
        Hyperkalemia (potassium >5.5mEq/L)
        Hypokalemia (potassium <3.5mEq/L)

    Petechiae   
        Thrombocytopenia (platelets <150,000)

    PNA symptoms    
        Neutropenia (WBC <1,500)

    Presyncope  
        Polycythemia (hemoglobin trending upward)

    Reflexes    
        Hypercalcemia (calcium) ~ decreased
        Hypocalcemia (calcium) ~ increased
        Hypokalemia (potassium <3.5mEq/L) ~ decreased
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L) ~ decreased

    Seizure     
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L)
        Hypocalcemia (calcium)
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)
        Polycythemia (hemoglobin trending upward)

    Shaking 
        Hypoglycemia (glucose <70)

    Skin    
        Blood urea nitrogen (kidney >25mg/dL) ~ itchy/dry
        Neutropenia (WBC <1,500) ~ abscesses

    SOB 
        Leukopenia (WBC <4,000)

    Sore mouth  
        Neutropenia (WBC <1,500)

    Splenomegaly    
        Thrombocytopenia (platelets <150,000)

    Swelling / edema    
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L)
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L) ~ pitting edema
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward) ~ edema

    Tachycardia     
        Anemia / downward trend of hemoglobin
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L)

    TIA symptoms    
        Polycythemia (hemoglobin trending upward)

    Tingling    
        Hypocalcemia (calcium) ~ numbness or tingling
        Thrombocytosis (platelets >450,000) ~ hands/feet

    Urinary output  
        Hypernatremia (sodium >145mEq/L) ~ decreased
        Serum creatinine (kidney - trending upward) ~ reduced and/or dark colored

    Weakness    
        Anemia
        Hypercalcemia (calcium) ~ muscle
        Hyperkalemia (potassium >5.5mEq/L) ~ weakness or paralysis
        Hypoglycemia (glucose <70) ~ extremity weakness
        Hypokalemia (potassium <3.5mEq/L) ~ extremity weakness
        Hyponatremia (sodium <130mEq/L)
        Leukopenia (WBC <4,000)
        Thrombocytosis (platelets >450,000)

    Weight loss 
        Leukocytosis (WBC >11,000)

    OTHER NOTES:
        Hypercalcemia can be caused from consumption of too much calcium or break down of bone via osteoclasts
        While other elements can create cardiac arrhythmias, a troponin level above 0.10 ng/mL is the GOLD STANDARD for diagnosing an MI
            However, troponin levels can be elevated for other reasons, one of that being when renal failure is occurring
                -Kidneys regulate fluid retention in the body which affects the blood urea nitrogen levels
                -If the kidneys go into failure, the heart has to work harder to pump the fluid to the rest of the body and can cause cardiac damage
                -Kidneys also work to regulate blood pressure so if the organs aren’t functioning properly or at all, this can cause hypertension
                    -If there is a low cardiac output from the heart, they 
                -Another function of the kidneys is to regulate the amount of salt that’s in the body and filter out the excess. If the salt is not being excreted, this can cause hypernatremia which then leads to hypertension 
        -Hyper- and hypo-glycemia would need to be monitored in someone who has cystic fibrosis-related diabetes
            -Symptoms would be excessive fatigue, confusion, and dizziness

    CHAPTER 8 - Cardiovascular Diagnostic Tests and Procedures
        Table 8-2 - Clinical Laboratory Studies with Normative Values
            .Denomination
                Measurement → Normative Values
            ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
            .Serum enzymes and cardiac biomarkers
                Creatine phosphokinase (CPK) 5–75 mU/mL
                CPK-MB isoenzyme 0%–3%
                Lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) 100–225 mU/mL
                Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 10–40 mU/dL
                Troponin <0.2 µg/mL
                    troponin I: 0–0.1 ng/mL (onset: 4–6 hours, peak)
                    troponin T: 0–0.2 ng/mL (onset: 3–4 hours)
                Myoglobin <100 ng/mL onset 1–3 hours
                    Male: 10–95 ng/mL
                    Female: 10–65 ng/mL
                Blood natriuretic peptide (BNP) <100 pg/mL Normal
                    <500 Goal at hospital discharge
                    ≥700 Decompensated congested heart failure
                    ≈3000 During nesiritide infusion
                Carbonic anhydrase III Myo/CAIII <3.2

            .Blood lipids
                Total cholesterol <200 mg/dL
                High-density lipoproteins (HDL) Male: ≥40 mg/dL
                Female: ≥50 mg/dL
                Low-density lipoproteins (LDL) <100 mg/dL
                Triglycerides <140 mg/dL

            .Other risk factors for coronary artery disease (CAD)
                Homocysteine ≤13.0 µmol/L
                C-reactive protein hs-(CRP)
                    Low risk <1.0 mg/L
                    Avg risk 1.0–3.0 mg/L
                    High risk >3.0 mg/L
                    If >10.0 mg/L eval for other problems
                Glucose 70–110 mg/dL
                HbA1C ≤6.0%

            .Complete blood cell count
                Red blood cells (RBC)
                    Males: 4.6–6.2 × 106/µL
                    Females: 4.2–5.4 × 104/µL
                Hemoglobin (HgB)
                    Male: 13.5–18 g/dL
                    Female: 12–16 g/dL
                Hematocrit (Hct)
                    Male: 40%–54%
                    Female: 38%–47%
                White blood cells (WBC) 4500–11,000/µL of whole blood
                Platelets 300,000/µL

            .Coagulation profile
                Prothrombin time 11.6–13.0 s
                Partial thromboplastin time 21.5–34.1 s
                International Normalized Ratio 
                (INR)
                    Prevention /treatment of venous thrombosis or PE 2.0–3.0
                    Prosthetic heart valves 2.5–3.5
                    Prevention of recurrent MI 2.5–3.5

            .Electrolytes, Others
                Na+ 136–143 mEq/L
                K+ 3.8–5.0 mEq/L
                Blood urea nitrogen 8–18 mg/dL
                Creatinine 0.6–1.2 mg/dL
                Albumin >2.5 g

        Myo/CAIII = myoglobin value/carbonic anhydrase III.
